barrier.config: the config file (core/data/mixdog-config.json): config/setTheme with the theme config/getTheme answered at the first look, which mixdog-core-config writes through the config's one writer (config/mod.rs Config::update on its write lane, written even when unchanged, as Node's updateConfig) and answers once written; a config write the refused call queued is written before it. Its answer must name the theme
barrier.mcpServerList: in the config file: mcp/addMcpServer and mcp/saveMcpServer write the list through that same writer (mixdog-mcp mcp_service.rs save_servers -> save_config -> Config::update), so the config step covers it
barrier.prompts: the prompt-history files (core/data/tui-prompt-history): part of the session step (the appends a thread pushed before the call are written)
barrier.secretsStore: no step: a secret is written on the durability lane inside the call that writes it and before that call answers (mixdog-secrets lib.rs on_lane, windows.rs DpapiStore::set); nothing is queued past the answer
barrier.sessionStore: replay/storesSettled, sent as a raw frame from the paired phone after the config step's answer (the desktop's protocol client sends only the method table's methods), a development-build control (mixdog-cli feature replay-controls; refused in a release build by build.rs): each thread loaded when it arrives takes its accept watermark then (the last record its actor accepted, the prompt-history appends pushed) and answers once every record up to it is committed - written and synced by the store, which acks it (mixdog-store log.rs append_barrier sync_file; mixdog-core-session actor.rs on_durability -> Outbox::acked) - and every append up to it is written (prompt_history.rs AppendQueue::marks); records accepted later neither hold nor hasten it, a thread loaded later is not asked, and one unloaded meanwhile counts once its close flushed (directory.rs SessionDirectory::durability_settled, actor.rs answer_settled). A record or append from before it that failed (outbox.rs Outbox::note_failed) answers an error naming the thread. Within a 20 s deadline that fails the call with what it waited for (mixdog-app-server-daemon replay_stores_settled.rs). Its answer must hold the number of threads asked; an error fails the replay with its message
barrier.writeBehind: the same replay/storesSettled call, around the session step, with one shape for every writer (mixdog-rt write_marks.rs WriteMarks: each write numbered as accepted and reported written or failed; the call takes each writer's accepted count as it arrives and waits for its committed count to reach it, so writes accepted later neither hold nor hasten it, and a write from before it that failed answers an error naming the store): the agent index's row writes (mixdog-core-session agent_registry StoreWorkers::marks, which hand header changes to the threads before the session step), the read-state snapshots under core/data/read-snapshots (mixdog-tools read_state.rs ReadState::marks, their debounce cut short by ReadState::flush_pending), the gateway usage events in core/data/gateway-usage.local.jsonl (gateway_usage store.rs GatewayUsage::marks, then GatewayUsage::compact_scheduled_now), and the usage ledger when it is open (mixdog-ledger writer.rs UsageWriter::marks)

skip.reason: the core's ownership of its data folder: an OS-held exclusive lock for its whole life (Node's daemon-owner.lock likewise), so its bytes cannot be read while it runs; written once at the start

the barrier's own config write (worldFiles.barrier) adds a pre- and a post-config-write copy of the config here each time, as every config write does (Node's user-data-backup likewise); a config write by the refused call would change the config file itself (mixdog-config.json), which is compared

the core's diagnostic log: lines from its own timers and events (a language server it stops when idle, for one), not stored state; a refused call is answered before any service runs, so it logs nothing a service would
the models.dev catalog cache: refreshed by the core on its own schedule from models.dev (not a stand-in server), as Node's catalog refresh does; no client call writes it

the lock the models.dev catalog's refresh holds while it writes the cache (the entry above), with the record it stages and the guard it takes to reclaim a stale one (mixdog-statefile lock.rs publish_lock, reclaim)

the npm registry's latest version, cached 24 h by the core's own update check (mixdog-core-domains update.rs, Node's self-update.mjs) from registry.npmjs.org (not a stand-in server), written whenever that check, started by the core at its start, answers

the last answer of each provider CLI's live version lookup (mixdog-ai client_versions.rs, Node's live CLI versions): written when a lookup the core started on its own answers, from the providers' sites (not a stand-in server); no client call writes it

the lock the live version lookup holds while it writes its cache (the entry above), with the record it stages and the guard it takes to reclaim a stale one (mixdog-statefile lock.rs publish_lock, reclaim)
